Coverage notes: Statutory general government sector agencies in Schedule 1 Part 1 (government agencies) and Part 2 (legislative agencies), current as at the last applied amendment (No. 30 of 2025, 8 October 2026).

Source name: Tasmanian State Service Careers – Our agencies
Coverage notes: Named State Service departments and state authorities on the careers 'Our agencies' page. The page names 17 agencies (plus Service Tasmania, which was treated as a service brand and omitted).

Eight directorates, listed public sector bodies and statutory authorities, and Icon Water (territory-owned corporation). Official Website Address values are taken from the agency links on this page (including a small number of official .com.au / .edu.au sites listed there). The ACT Directory (directory.act.gov.au) was not used because that site warns it still reflects pre-1 July 2025 structures.

Source name: Administrative Arrangements Order 2026, Schedule 1 – Nomination of Agencies
Coverage notes: Agencies nominated in Schedule 1: Part 1 (Financial Management Act and Public Sector Employment and Management Act), Part 2 (Financial Management Act only) and Part 3 (Public Sector Employment and Management Act only). Made 27 May 2026; commenced and gazetted S41 on 1 June 2026. Does not attempt to list every non-agency body mentioned in Schedule 2. The Order does not publish ABNs or websites.

Australian Business Register public bulk extract on data.gov.au (CC BY 3.0 AU), files public_split_1_10.zip and public_split_11_20.zip dated 11 November 2026. Used to look up ABNs for non-Commonwealth entities. Only Active (ABN status ACT) records whose EntityTypeInd is a government type (CG*, SG*, TG*, LG*, plus GOV, SSA, STA, TER, LOC) were eligible. A match is accepted only when the entity name matches confidently and the recorded state agrees with the jurisdiction (or, for a long distinctive name, the match is unique nationally). Confidence is 'exact' for a unique in-state match on the normalised legal/trading name, or 'high' for a unique match after light name-variant normalisation. Ambiguous or weak hits are left blank. Other entity types (for example Australian Public Company, Other Incorporated Entity) are not used, so universities and some state-owned corporations may have no ABN even when one exists. Websites are not present in the extract.
